sentences.text: A s per the case of prosecution, Vishnu s/o Jeevaram Kushhwah submitted a typed complaint to SHO, PS Panihar on 27/02/2024 inter-alia stating that in year 2009 to 2010, Vijay Singh s/o Natharam proposed to double the invested amount in insurance policy.
He paid Rs. Four Lacs to Vijay Singh (applicant).
Vijay Singh gave one fixed deposit receipt of Shri Ram Finance Company to him.
On completion of tenure of fixed deposit, he approached Vijay Singh.
Vijay Singh taken his six FDs but he did not pay him maturity amount and fled away from the village.
Vijay Singh has committed cheating with Ghanshayam, Mayaram Kushwah, Smt. Prembai, Damodar Kushwah and Uma Kushwah also.
On such allegations, PS Panihar registered FIR at Crime No. 31/2024 for offence punishable under Section 420 of the IPC.
Statements of witnesses were recorded.
Applicant was arrested on 28/02/2024, he is in custody ever since.
In his statement recorded under Section 27 of the Evidence Act, Vijay Singh stated that he was working as Agent of Shri Ram Real Estate Company owned by Nirmal Dhaneliya and Sanjay Mevad.
The company used to pay him 5% of invested amount, therefore, he had opened the accounts of various residents of Village Tighara and deposited the amount with Conmpany.
He had given receipts of the policies to the concerned villagers.
He himself has invested in the company but owners of the company closed the office and fled away.
Certain policies were recovered at the instance of applicant.
Investigation is underway.

Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant himself is victim of fraud and cheating by owners of Shriram Real Estate Company namely Nirmal Dhaneliya and Sanjay Mevad.
He had invested money of other villagers and himself in the company but owners of the company fled away, therefore, no payment could be made.

Referring to FIR at crime No.63/2017 of Police Station Inderganj, District Gwalior, learned counsel submit that applicant has submitted a written complaint whereupon FIR dated 06/02/2017 was registered against Sanjay Singh Mevad, Nirmal Singh, Jagdish Meena, Chand Singh, Deepak Dangi,
Arvind Jadon and Vijay Singh Chandel.
Learned counsel contends that there was no intention to defraud the complainant and other villagers on the part of the applicant from inception.

Therefore,
no offence as alleged is made out against the applicant.
Applicant is aged 45 years.
He has family to look after.
There is no likelihood of his obsconsion leaving his family and home.
No criminal antecedents is reported against the applicant.
There is no likelihood of tampering with evidence by the applicant.
Trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
